objective.value: Propose and validate a design logic for transcriptional repressor-based genetic inverters; as proof of concept, construct a tryptophan-inducible TrpR-TetR genetic inverter in Escherichia coli, optimize its dynamic performance, and apply derived tryptophan-triggered regulation systems to monitor tryptophan production and dynamically regulate tryptamine and violacein production.

value: Coupling a ligand-inducible transcriptional repressor (TrpR1, sensing tryptophan) to control expression of a second repressor (TetR) can invert the repression output into a tryptophan-inducible activation output.
Attaching protein degradation tags (DAS/DSA, LAA) to TetR would reduce TetR protein stability and relieve the stringent repression of PtetO1, restoring dose-dependent regulation.
Reducing TetR abundance (via weaker RBS) and increasing PtetO1 promoter strength would amplify inverter activation output.
Tryptophan-triggered dynamic (bifunctional) regulation of heterologous pathways would improve tryptamine and violacein titers relative to constitutive static controls.
hypothesis.notes: Hypotheses are stated at multiple points (design logic in section 1; explicit 'we hypothesized' for degradation tags in section 2; factor identification in section 3). Document-level projection merges several instance-level hypotheses; see experimental_design_object for per-experiment binding.

value: Inverter_V1 showed no significant RFP activation; dysfunction attributed to stringent TetR-PtetO1 repression.
Inverter_V1.1 (TetR_DSA): 3.2-fold dynamic range, 40.8+/-7.8 to 129.6+/-53.0 a.u.; Inverter_V1.2 (TetR_LAA): 14.7-fold dynamic range, leaky 45.8+/-4.7 a.u., max 672.6+/-142.2 a.u.
RBS engineering: Inverter_V1.2.1 (RBS(G7T)) reached 2208+/-5.0 a.u. (5-fold over 440+/-21.1 a.u. baseline); Inverter_V1.1.1 showed 7.38-fold dynamic range.

PtetO1 engineering: PtetO1-RBS(A2C) gave 2.21-fold RFP over wildtype; Inverter_V1.2.1e reached 2316.3+/-75.5 a.u. (4.8-fold range, leaky 483.8+/-22.6); Inverter_V1.1.1e reached 1485.1+/-48.5 a.u. (6.8-fold range, leaky 218.6+/-40.5).

XG3 repression efficiency 96.67% vs 73.07% control (Figure S3); Inverter_V2.1.1 showed 10.7-fold dynamic range (leaky 380.8+/-56.1 a.u.); V2.1.1e 14.2-fold/5316.5+/-241.4 a.u.; V2.2.1e 3.4-fold/5649.1+/-273.9 a.u.; V2.1.1f 13.2-fold/2696.8+/-92.8 a.u.; V2.2.1f 3.3-fold/2558.1+/-67.6 a.u.
Dual_V2.1.1 and Dual_V2.2.1 showed simultaneous RFP activation and GFP repression; single-cell imaging showed no crosstalk between modules.
Monitoring strains tracked tryptophan production during fermentation (full activation at 42 h; TRPdual_LAA bifunctionality from 30 h).
Tryptamine: TM_Low reached 36.9+/-2.8 mg/L at 48 h, 2.0-fold over TM_Control.
Violacein: Vio_LH and Vio_HH exceeded control by 4.5-fold and 5.7-fold; Viodual_HH reached 10.5+/-0.6 mg/L, 7.4-fold over Vio_0.5 (1.4+/-0.1 mg/L) and 1.3-fold over Vio_HH-0.5 (8.0+/-0.4 mg/L).

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Authors actively designed and assembled a two-repressor cascade inverter architecture with copy-number-graded plasmid allocation.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Assembled Inverter_V1: constitutive Plpp0.03-TrpR1(V58K) on low-copy pSA74; PtrpO1(G3C)-tetR on medium-copy pCS27; PtetO1-RFP reporter on high-copy pZE12; TrpR1 as sensor repressor 1, TetR as output repressor 2.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Design logic: repressor 1 detects inducer and controls repressor 2; repressor 2 executes and inverts the signal (Results section 1).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Transcriptional repressors are mono-functional and their applications are limited by repression-only output and leaky expression (Introduction), motivating functional inversion.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent: component choice PtrpO1(G3C)-TrpR1(V58K) from authors' prior study (Gong et al., 2022); PtetO1-TetR from Lutz and Bujard, 1997. Cascade logic itself is authors' proposal, not prior-validated.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Specific repressor variant selected 'based on its low leaky expression and high repression efficacy when induced by tryptophan in our previous study (Gong et al., 2022)'.

generalizable_rule.rule: A ligand-inducible transcriptional repressor controlling expression of a second repressor can invert a repression output into an inducible activation output.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: TrpR1(V58K)/TetR pair with tryptophan in E. coli BW25113-derived strains XG1/XG3, three- or two-plasmid configurations, M9-2Y, 24 h tube assays
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other repressor pairs, other ligands, other hosts, and in-vivo production conditions not tested for the generic logic

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Attaching protein degradation tags to TetR was an explicit engineering action taken to fix Inverter_V1 dysfunction.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Fused DAS/DSA or LAA degradation tags to TetR, generating PtetO1-TetR variant systems and inverter variants Inverter_V1.1 (TetR_DSA) and Inverter_V1.2 (TetR_LAA).
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Stated hypothesis: reduced TetR protein stability would relieve the stringent repression of PtetO1.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Inverter_V1 showed no significant RFP activation; isolated PtetO1-TetR testing showed extreme repression at low IPTG without dose-dependent response (Figure S1b), attributed to strong TetR-PtetO1 binding.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement: trigger from fluorescence assays (Figure 1e, Figure S1b/c; S1 data in supplement, not provided).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Mechanistic rationale (lower TetR stability relieves stringent repression) was stated before variant construction and then tested.

generalizable_rule.rule: Fusing faster-degrading ssrA-type tags (e.g., LAA) to TetR can convert stringent TetR-PtetO1 repression into dose-dependent, relievable repression and rescue a non-functional two-repressor inverter.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: TetR/PtetO1 in E. coli XG1, IPTG 0-50 uM titration and tryptophan 0-500 mg/L inverter assays
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other repressor-operator pairs, other degradation tags, other hosts

alternatives_considered: DAS/DSA tag (slower degradation) implemented in parallel as Inverter_V1.1; LAA gave higher output and was carried forward

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: RBS engineering of the sensor-repressor cassette was a deliberate design action to reduce TetR accumulation.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Random mutagenesis of RBS positions 6-9 driving the PtrpO1(G3C) system; screened variants; selected RBS(G7T), RBS(A8G), RBS(G9C) to build Inverter_V1.1.1-3 and V1.2.1-3.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Reduce leaky expression of the TrpR1(V58K) repression system to lower TetR abundance and relieve continuous tight repression of PtetO1.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Inverter variants V1.1/V1.2 showed low expression levels, attributed to leaky TrpR1 expression causing excessive TetR accumulation (Results section 3).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=screening_result plus experimental_measurement (Figure S2 screen, Figure 2b/c characterization).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Mechanistic chain (leakiness -> TetR accumulation -> tight PtetO1 repression -> low output) stated before the intervention; variant selection was screening-guided.

generalizable_rule.rule: Weakening the RBS driving the sensor repressor reduces inverter leakiness and amplifies activation output in a two-repressor cascade.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: PtrpO1(G3C) RBS positions 6-9 variants in XG1-based inverters with tetR_DSA/tetR_LAA
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other promoters/RBS contexts, other hosts, untested RBS positions

alternatives_considered: RBS(G6C) and RBS(A8T) variants were generated but not selected for inverter optimization (lower leakiness criterion)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: PtetO1 promoter/RBS engineering was a deliberate action to raise output expression levels.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Random mutagenesis of the PtetO1 -10 region and its RBS; variants (N4-2, N4-14, N6-8, N6-15, RBS(A2C/G6C/A8G)) introduced into Inverter_V1.1.1/V1.2.1 generating a-g series.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Weak PtetO1 promoter strength was identified as a direct cause of low activation output.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Low expression levels of inverter variants after degradation-tag and RBS optimization (Results section 3, first paragraph).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=screening_result: relative RFP of promoter variants (Figure 2e) and inverter characterization (Figure 2f/g).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Stated causal attribution (weak promoter strength -> low output) preceded the intervention.

generalizable_rule.rule: Increasing output-promoter (PtetO1) strength raises inverter activation output, with activation strength correlating with promoter variant strength.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: PtetO1 variants in XG1-based Inverter_V1.1.1/V1.2.1 series
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other output promoters, other circuit architectures, other hosts

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: ubiC knockout is a deliberate host-engineering action to supply the inducer intracellularly.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Deleted ubiC in XG1 (P1 transduction) to create tryptophan-producing strain XG2.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: ubiC catalyzes chorismate-to-4-hydroxybenzoate conversion and bypasses the tryptophan pathway; deletion directs more carbon flux toward tryptophan.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Circuit implementation requires in-host supply of the inducer (tryptophan) rather than exogenous addition (Results section 4).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=stoichiometric_constraint (pathway rerouting rationale stated in text); tryptophan overproduction confirmed indirectly in later fermentation experiments.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Pathway-level mechanistic rationale (competing chorismate bypass) stated at the time of the decision.

generalizable_rule.rule: Deleting ubiC increases intracellular tryptophan availability for self-supplied inducer of TrpR-based circuits.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: E. coli BW25113-derived XG1 background, M9-2Y glycerol medium, shake-flask and tube formats
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other carbon sources, other strain backgrounds, other chorismate-derived product contexts

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Chromosomal integration of TrpR1(V58K) is a deliberate configuration decision to reduce plasmid count.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Integrated Plpp0.03-TrpR(V58K)-T1 cassette into XG2 chromosome (lambda red recombination, ~100 bp downstream of a gene whose name was lost in parsing), yielding XG3; inverters rebuilt as two-plasmid systems (V2.x).
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Stated motivation: reduce the number of plasmids required by the three-plasmid inverter.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: The original inverter required three plasmids and two repressors, anticipated to cause plasmid-recruitment burden in applications (Results section 4).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement for the outcome (96.67% vs 73.07% repression efficiency; 10.7-fold improved dynamic range), though Figure S3 is supplement-dependent.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The paper reports a practical motivation (reducing plasmid number) but provides no mechanistic or literature-based justification for why integration would improve performance; contract enum has no 'practical rationale' value, so mapped to rationale_not_reported with this note (enum limitation recorded).

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Coupling the native TrpR1 repression output to the inverter as a bifunctional circuit is a deliberate design extension.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Added a PtrpO1(G3C)-controlled GFP operon to Inverter_V2.1.1/V2.2.1, creating Dual_V2.1.1/Dual_V2.2.1 with simultaneous activation (RFP) and repression (GFP).
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Reuse the inherent repression function of PtrpO1(G3C)-TrpR1(V58K) alongside the inverted activation output.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Successful performance of optimized two-plasmid inverters in XG3 (Figure 3a-c) preceded the bifunctional extension ('based on the results, we proposed...').
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The bifunctional design follows directly from the established topology in which the TrpR1-tryptophan complex represses PtrpO1(G3C)-driven targets.

generalizable_rule.rule: A TrpR-based inverter can be extended to simultaneous activation and repression by adding a PtrpO1(G3C)-controlled repression target, without observed inter-module crosstalk at single-cell level.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: Dual_V2.1.1/Dual_V2.2.1 in XG3, tryptophan gradient tube assays and light-sheet imaging
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other repressor systems, other effector molecules, untested target genes

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Adding an ASV degradation tag to the RFP reporter is a deliberate design choice for dynamic monitoring.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Fused ASV degradation tag to the RFP reporter of Inverter_V2.1.1/V2.2.1, generating monitoring strains TRPactive_DSA and TRPactive_LAA.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Alleviate RFP accumulation so reporter dynamics track tryptophan production during fermentation.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Need to monitor metabolite formation during fermentation in real time (citing Rogers and Church, 2016; Rogers et al., 2015).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent for tag utility (McGinness et al., 2006) plus experimental_measurement of monitoring performance (Figure 4).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Mechanistic rationale (faster reporter turnover reduces accumulation) stated at design time.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Introducing the PLlacO1-trpE_fbrG operon is a deliberate intervention to boost tryptophan supply.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Inserted an additional PLlacO1-controlled trpE_fbrG operon into the medium-copy plasmid of monitoring/regulation strains; induced with 0.5 mM IPTG.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Boost tryptophan generation in the host strain.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Implementation of the inverter for production monitoring requires sufficient endogenous tryptophan formation.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (tryptophan titers and reporter response in Figure 4 fermentations).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Overexpressing feedback-resistant trpE (trpE_fbr) with trpG to increase tryptophan biosynthesis is a pathway-level mechanistic rationale stated in text ('to boost tryptophan generation').

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Replacing the RFP reporter with CrTDC under low/high dynamic promoters is a deliberate pathway-regulation design.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Built TM_Low (PtetO1-RBS(A8G)-CrTDC) and TM_High (PtetO1-RBS(A2C)-CrTDC) in TRPactive_DSA; compared against constitutive Plpp0.5-CrTDC control.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Two-stage dynamic regulation: low tryptophan early keeps synthase low; accumulating tryptophan activates CrTDC to convert tryptophan to tryptamine.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: TRPactive_DSA shown to monitor tryptophan production and to respond specifically to tryptophan over tryptamine (Figure S5), enabling tryptophan-triggered activation of a downstream pathway.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (titers, Figure 5b); CrTDC source is literature_precedent (Wang et al., 2020; plasmid pTY4).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: CrTDC enzyme and tryptamine pathway adopted from Wang et al., 2020; dynamic-regulation rationale is authors' mechanistic framing.

generalizable_rule.rule: Low-level tryptophan-triggered dynamic activation of CrTDC outperformed both high-level dynamic activation and strength-matched constitutive overexpression for tryptamine production.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: TRPactive_DSA-derived strains in XG3, M9-2Y glycerol, 30 C, 48 h shake flasks
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other enzymes/pathways, other hosts, other dynamic ranges, scale-up

alternatives_considered: High-level dynamic activation (TM_High) and static constitutive overexpression (TM_Control) were implemented and compared; low-level dynamic gave the highest titer

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Selecting plsB as the dynamic down-regulation target for violacein bifunctional regulation is an explicit, justified design choice.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Constructed PtrpO1(G3C)-plsB repression operon in Vio_HH to create Viodual_HH, combining dynamic up-regulation of vio operons with dynamic down-regulation of plsB.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Expected sequence: initial plsB expression supports membrane buildup and cell growth, later repression shifts resources toward violacein formation.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Observed repression pattern of the bifunctional system (target initially increases, then decreases; Figure 4e) plus literature report that plsB overexpression improved deoxyviolacein production (Yang et al., 2021).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent for target choice (Yang et al., 2021, deoxyviolacein analog) combined with experimental_measurement of the outcome (Figure 5f).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Explicit analogy: 'Considering the similar chemical property of deoxyviolacein and violacein, plsB was selected as our dynamic down-regulation target.'

generalizable_rule.rule: For hydrophobic membrane-accumulating indole pigments, dynamically down-regulating plsB (initial expression then repression) alongside dynamic pathway up-regulation can improve titer over static controls.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: violacein in XG3-derived Viodual_HH, M9-2Y, 30 C, 48 h shake flasks
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: other products, other membrane targets, other hosts, other fermentation scales

alternatives_considered: Single up-regulation with constitutive plsB (Vio_HH-0.5) and unregulated (Vio_0.5) configurations were implemented as controls and gave lower titers

candidate_values: TetR degradation tag named 'DAS' (Results section 2: 'we introduced two protein degradation tags DAS and LAA'; 'TetR_DAS and TetR_LAA into Inverter_V1')
TetR degradation tag named 'DSA' (Methods 2_dna_manipulation_p002: 'attaching the DSA or LAA protein degradation tags'; Figure 1/2/4 captions: 'DSA degradation tag'; strain name TRPactive_DSA)
conflicts.conflict_reason: Results text uses 'DAS' while Methods, figure captions and strain names use 'DSA' for the same tetR degradation tag; cannot silently pick one spelling.
conflicts.review_action: Check original PDF/supplement sequences to determine the intended tag name (likely a DAS/DSA variant of the ssrA tag); keep both spellings linked to the same construct until resolved.

candidate_values: Inverter_V1.2.1 described as '5-fold increase from the baseline of 440+/-21.1 a.u.' (Results section 3), implying a V1.2 baseline of 440 a.u.
conflicts.conflict_reason: The 440+/-21.1 a.u. baseline cited for the 5-fold improvement of Inverter_V1.2.1 does not match the earlier reported 672.6+/-142.2 a.u. maximum for Inverter_V1.2; may reflect different experimental batches or a different reference condition, but this is not explained in the text.
conflicts.review_action: Compare Figure 1e and Figure 2c raw data (or source data) to determine whether the baselines come from different assay batches; do not merge the two values.
